title.narrative: Strengthening National Capacity for Public Monitoring of Local Government Reforms

description.narrative: The proposed grant will support BAPPENAS (the National Development Agency) in the development of an independent monitoring system that will monitor and benchmark the local government reform program, especially in the areas of financial management and procurement, and record its impact on the citizens. To achieve independent monitoring, BAPPENAS will work closely with CSOs, including NGOs and universities. Over a period of three years the grant will help establish independent monitoring structures in some twenty locations and thereby develop a replicable system for the rest of Indonesia. The funds will also be used to strengthen the capacity of these structures to undertake their monitoring functions effectively. In particular, the grant will support monitoring of specific governance reform improvements through effective indicators and indices. To make sense of the information reaching the national level, it will be necessary to establish an MIS that can effectively filter incoming data. It is expected that at least 10 districts/municipalities will adopt the new mechanism during the life of the grant, and at least 20 others will adopt the mechanisms within 2 years of the grant closing. The outcome of this will be that national level government will be able to better understand the level of reform in participating districts/municipalities and the problems faced. This, in turn should lead to more effective strategies of suppor for the reformers. Overall, the expected outcomes will be reflected in more appropriate national support to the decentralization effort, as a result of the improved capacity of BAPPENAS to gain and evaluate more objective district level information from the strengthened linkages with the CSOs. In terms of long term sustainability, the channels of communication created between participating districts/municipalities and BAPPENAS will require minimum effort to maintain, from the local CSOs and from BAPPENAS. The subtle shift in power, with CSOs empowered to provide suggestions and complaints direct to symphatetic listeners at national level, will in itself motivate these institutions to remain engage in the dialog.
